items.title: Confidence sets and coverage
items.statement: A confidence-set procedure C:X→2^Theta has measurable membership sections C_eta={x:eta∈C(x)} for every eta. Under a nonempty experiment (X,A,(P_theta)), its coverage at theta is P_theta(C_theta), and its confidence level is the infimum of coverage over theta. Coverage is at least 1-alpha when every P_theta(C_theta)≥1-alpha.

references.title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT 14.381, Lecture 11: Confidence Sets, §1, PDF p. 1
Karl B. Gregory, USC STAT 713, Lecture 14: Confidence Intervals and Sets, slides 2–3, PDF pp. 2–4

items.title: Pivotal quantities
items.statement: A family of measurable maps q_theta:X→S is a pivot in an experiment (X,A,(P_theta)) when the pushforward laws P_theta(q_theta^{-1}(·)) are one common probability measure on S. No measurability in the parameter is assumed.

references.title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT 14.381, Lecture 11: Confidence Sets, §2, PDF pp. 2–3
Karl B. Gregory, USC STAT 713, Lecture 14: Confidence Intervals and Sets, slide 6, PDF p. 6

items.title: Coverage from pivot inversion and exact calibration
items.statement: If q_theta is a pivot with common law nu and B is measurable with nu(B)≥1-alpha, then C(x)={theta:q_theta(x)∈B} has coverage at least 1-alpha. Equality nu(B)=1-alpha gives exact coverage. For interval acceptance sets with atoms, calibrate nu([a,b]) itself.
items.strategy: Direct. Each membership section is the measurable preimage q_theta^{-1}(B), and its probability is nu(B) for every theta.

references.title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT 14.381, Lecture 11: Confidence Sets, §2, PDF pp. 2–3
Karl B. Gregory, USC STAT 713, Lecture 14: Confidence Intervals and Sets, slides 6 and 9, PDF pp. 6 and 14

items.title: Coverage from test inversion
items.statement: For each eta in a nonempty parameter set, let A_eta be a measurable point-null acceptance event on the full observation space, including any auxiliary randomization, and assume Q_eta(A_eta)>=1-alpha. Then C(y)={eta:y in A_eta} is a confidence set with coverage at least 1-alpha.
items.strategy: Direct. The membership section for eta is exactly A_eta, so its coverage under the true law is the acceptance probability of that point-null test.

references.title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT 14.381, Lecture 11: Confidence Sets, §2, PDF p. 1
Karl B. Gregory, USC STAT 713, Lecture 14: Confidence Intervals and Sets, slide 12, PDF p. 20

items.title: A discrete pivot can give conservative coverage
items.statement: On the integer location model X=theta+Z with Z uniform on {-1,0,1}, the pivot X-theta has a parameter-free three-atom law. At nominal level 4/5, inversion of B=[-1,1] gives C(X)={X-1,X,X+1}, whose coverage is 1 because B contains all pivot atoms.
items.strategy: Direct finite verification. Normalize the three-point law, compute the pivot distribution, invert its central acceptance set, and calculate coverage including the atoms.

references.title: Karl B. Gregory, USC STAT 713, Lecture 14: Confidence Intervals and Sets, slide 9, PDF p. 14

items.title: Known-variance normal mean interval
items.statement: Assume AC and observe Y∼N(mu,sigma^2), mu∈R, known sigma>0. For 0<alpha<1 the interval [Y-z_{1-alpha/2}sigma,Y+z_{1-alpha/2}sigma] has exact coverage 1-alpha.
items.strategy: Direct. Prove existence of the normal quantile, calculate its symmetric acceptance probability, and invert the standardized normal pivot.

references.title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT 14.381, Lecture 11: Confidence Sets, §2, PDF pp. 1–3
Karl B. Gregory, USC STAT 713, Lecture 14: Confidence Intervals and Sets, slide 8, PDF p. 10

items.title: Exact unknown-variance normal t interval
items.statement: Assume AC and iid N(mu,lambda) observations with n>=2. Restrict the normal product law to the full-measure Borel set where the sample standard deviation is positive. For every fixed lambda>0, inversion of the exact t_(n-1) pivot gives the usual mean interval with coverage 1-alpha.
items.strategy: Conditional on the named MSF-35 suppliers: establish existence and calibration of t quantiles from the t-law representation, then invert the exact normal mean-residual pivot. Supplier body and proof remain to be checked.

references.title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT 14.381, Lecture 11: Confidence Sets, §2, PDF p. 3
Karl B. Gregory, USC STAT 713, Lecture 14: Confidence Intervals and Sets, slides 8 and 12, PDF pp. 10 and 20

items.title: Uniform maximum pivot interval
items.statement: For n≥1 independent Uniform(0,theta) observations and M=max_i X_i, P_theta(M/theta≤u)=u^n for 0≤u≤1. The interval [M,M/alpha^(1/n)] has exact coverage 1-alpha for 0<alpha<1.
items.strategy: Direct. Measurability of the maximum and the product law give the parameter-free pivot cdf; invert the calibrated acceptance set [alpha^(1/n),1].

references.title: Karl B. Gregory, USC STAT 713, Lecture 14: Confidence Intervals and Sets, slide 9, Uniform maximum pivot exercise, PDF p. 14

items.title: Binomial upper confidence limit by lower-tail test inversion
items.statement: For X∼Bin(n,p), define F_p(k)=P_p(X≤k). The lower-tail level-alpha tests reject p=p0 when F_{p0}(X)<alpha. Inverting them gives C(X)=[0,U_X], where F_{U_k}(k)=alpha for k<n and U_n=1; coverage is at least 1-alpha.
items.strategy: Differentiate the binomial cdf to show strict decrease in p, establish unique upper endpoints, verify the finite tests have size at most alpha, and apply the local test-inversion theorem.

references.title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT 14.381, Lecture 11: Confidence Sets, §2, PDF p. 1
Karl B. Gregory, USC STAT 713, Lecture 14: Confidence Intervals and Sets, slide 12, PDF p. 20
